title: látlak, hallak: I Can See You, I Can Hear You

sections.title: One word for "I … you"
sections.content: You know the *-lak/-lek* ending from Unit 38: one word for "I … you", as in *szeretlek*. A video call is full of it: *látlak* ("I can see you") and *hallak* ("I can hear you"). For several people, add *titeket* (also Unit 38): *Látlak titeket.* The negative puts *nem* in front: *Nem hallak.* ("I can't hear you.") When the call fails, use *majd* from Unit 11 for a plan: *Majd felhívlak.* ("I'll phone you later.")

items.english: I can see you, but I can't hear you.

items.spanish: Hallak titeket, de nem látlak titeket.
items.english: I can hear you all, but I can't see you all.
The call was cut off, I'll phone you later.

sections.content: With *téged* or *titeket* as the object, the verb takes *-lak/-lek*: *Látlak*, not *Látom téged*. *Látom* means "I see it, him or her".
